"""Git worktrees for parallel tasks: create, commit, merge back, clean up."""

import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

MergeResult = Literal["merged", "conflict"]


class WorktreeError(RuntimeError):
    """A git command failed in a way the caller must handle."""


def _git(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)


def _check(proc: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]) -> str:
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise WorktreeError(proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip())
    return proc.stdout


class WorktreeManager:
    def __init__(self, repo: Path, run_id: str, integration_branch: str = "main") -> None:
        self.repo = Path(repo)
        self.run_id = run_id
        self.integration_branch = integration_branch

    def branch(self, task_id: str) -> str:
        """harness/<run_id>/<task_id>"""
        return f"harness/{self.run_id}/{task_id}"

    def path(self, task_id: str) -> Path:
        """<repo>/.harness/worktrees/<task_id>"""
        return self.repo / ".harness" / "worktrees" / task_id

    def _ensure_excluded(self) -> None:
        out = _check(_git("rev-parse", "--git-common-dir", cwd=self.repo)).strip()
        common = Path(out)
        if not common.is_absolute():
            common = self.repo / common
        exclude = common / "info" / "exclude"
        exclude.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        existing = exclude.read_text() if exclude.exists() else ""
        if ".harness/" in existing.splitlines():
            return
        prefix = "" if not existing or existing.endswith("\n") else "\n"
        exclude.write_text(existing + prefix + ".harness/\n")

    def create(self, task_id: str, base: str | None = None) -> Path:
        """git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <base or integration_branch>. Raise WorktreeError
        (with git's stderr) if git fails, e.g. the branch or path already exists. Return the path.
        """
        self._ensure_excluded()
        path = self.path(task_id)
        _check(
            _git(
                "worktree",
                "add",
                "-b",
                self.branch(task_id),
                str(path),
                base or self.integration_branch,
                cwd=self.repo,
            )
        )
        return path

    def commit(self, task_id: str, message: str) -> bool:
        """git add -A, then commit in the worktree. Return False (and commit nothing) if there
        are no staged changes (`git diff --cached --quiet` exits 0), True after committing."""
        wt = self.path(task_id)
        _check(_git("add", "-A", cwd=wt))
        diff = _git("diff", "--cached", "--quiet", cwd=wt)
        if diff.returncode == 0:
            return False
        if diff.returncode != 1:
            raise WorktreeError(diff.stderr.strip())
        _check(_git("commit", "-m", message, cwd=wt))
        return True

    def merge(self, task_id: str) -> MergeResult:
        """In the worktree: git rebase <integration_branch>. On failure: git rebase --abort and
        return "conflict". Then in <repo>: git merge --ff-only <branch>; raise WorktreeError if
        that fails. Return "merged"."""
        wt = self.path(task_id)
        status = _check(_git("status", "--porcelain", cwd=wt))
        if status.strip():
            raise WorktreeError(f"uncommitted changes in {task_id}")
        rebase = _git("rebase", self.integration_branch, cwd=wt)
        if rebase.returncode != 0:
            _git("rebase", "--abort", cwd=wt)
            return "conflict"
        _check(_git("merge", "--ff-only", self.branch(task_id), cwd=self.repo))
        return "merged"

    def discard(self, task_id: str) -> None:
        """Remove this task's worktree and branch if they exist, so the task can start over.
        Every git failure here is ignored (the worktree or branch may not exist)."""
        path = self.path(task_id)
        _git("worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path), cwd=self.repo)
        _git("branch", "-D", self.branch(task_id), cwd=self.repo)
        _git("worktree", "prune", cwd=self.repo)
        if path.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(path)

    def cleanup(self) -> None:
        """git worktree remove --force every worktree under <repo>/.harness/worktrees (from
        `git worktree list --porcelain`), delete every branch under refs/heads/harness/<run_id>/
        (git branch -D), then git worktree prune."""
        root = (self.repo / ".harness" / "worktrees").resolve()
        listing = _check(_git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain", cwd=self.repo))
        for line in listing.splitlines():
            if not line.startswith("worktree "):
                continue
            wt = Path(line[len("worktree ") :]).resolve()
            if wt.parent == root or root in wt.parents:
                _check(_git("worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt), cwd=self.repo))
        refs = _check(
            _git(
                "for-each-ref",
                "--format=%(refname:short)",
                f"refs/heads/harness/{self.run_id}/",
                cwd=self.repo,
            )
        )
        for name in refs.split():
            _check(_git("branch", "-D", name, cwd=self.repo))
        _check(_git("worktree", "prune", cwd=self.repo))

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from harness.worktree import WorktreeError, WorktreeManager


def _repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    for args in (
        ["init", "-b", "main"],
        ["config", "user.email", "test@example.com"],
        ["config", "user.name", "Test"],
    ):
        subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    (repo / "README.md").write_text("line one\n")
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", "init"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
    return repo


def _out(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True
    ).stdout

"""Worker interface: one work order in, one agent session, one WorkerResult out."""

import inspect
import json
import re
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from claude_agent_sdk import (
    AssistantMessage,
    ClaudeAgentOptions,
    ResultMessage,
    TextBlock,
    query,
)
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError

from harness.config import MODEL_IDS, Tier
from harness.models import Usage, WorkOrder

WorkerStatus = Literal["done", "failed", "unknown", "error"]

SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / "prompts" / "worker_system.md"

WORKER_TOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("Read", "Edit", "Write", "Glob", "Grep", "Bash")

WORKER_ENV: dict[str, str] = {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS": "1",
}

QueryFn = Callable[..., AsyncIterator[Any]]

_JSON_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^```json[ \t]*\n(.*?)\n```[ \t]*$", re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)


class SelfReportedCommand(BaseModel):
    """One entry of the worker's self-reported `acceptance` list. Not trusted."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    cmd: str
    exit_code: int | None


class WorkerReport(BaseModel):
    """The final JSON block of a worker's reply, as the worker wrote it.
    Unknown extra keys are ignored."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")

    status: Literal["done", "failed"]
    summary: str
    files_changed: list[str]
    acceptance: list[SelfReportedCommand]
    notes: str


class WorkerResult(BaseModel):
    """What one worker attempt returns. `status` is the worker's own claim (or why there is
    none); the verifier decides pass or fail."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    status: WorkerStatus
    summary: str = ""
    files_changed: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    notes: str = ""
    self_acceptance: list[SelfReportedCommand] = Field(default_factory=list)
    usage: Usage = Field(default_factory=Usage)
    num_turns: int = 0
    duration_ms: int = 0
    session_id: str | None = None
    final_text: str = ""
    error: str | None = None

    @property
    def cost_usd(self) -> float:
        """The attempt's cost in USD: self.usage.cost_usd."""
        return self.usage.cost_usd


@runtime_checkable
class Worker(Protocol):
    async def run(
        self, order: WorkOrder, tier: Tier, cwd: Path, retry_feedback: str | None = None
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Run one attempt of `order` on `tier` in the worktree `cwd`. Model and SDK
        failures come back as status "error", never as an exception."""
        ...


def parse_report(text: str) -> WorkerReport | None:
    """Find every fenced block that opens with a line of exactly three backticks followed by
    `json` (optional trailing spaces or tabs) and closes with a line of three backticks. Take
    the LAST such block, json.loads its body and validate it as a WorkerReport. Return None
    if there is no such block, the body is not valid JSON, it is not a JSON object, or
    validation fails. Never raises. Text after the last block is ignored."""
    try:
        matches = _JSON_BLOCK.findall(text)
    except TypeError:
        return None
    if not matches:
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(matches[-1])
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        # ValueError covers json.JSONDecodeError and the int-digit limit error.
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    try:
        return WorkerReport.model_validate(data)
    except ValidationError:
        return None


def apply_report(result: WorkerResult, report: WorkerReport | None) -> WorkerResult:
    """Return a copy of `result` with summary, files_changed, notes and self_acceptance taken
    from `report` (acceptance -> self_acceptance). If report is None, return `result`
    unchanged. Never changes status, usage or the other fields."""
    if report is None:
        return result
    return result.model_copy(
        update={
            "summary": report.summary,
            "files_changed": list(report.files_changed),
            "notes": report.notes,
            "self_acceptance": [c.model_copy() for c in report.acceptance],
        }
    )


def load_system_prompt(shared_context: str = "") -> str:
    """Read SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH (UTF-8) and strip trailing whitespace. If shared_context.strip()
    is non-empty, append "\\n\\n## Shared context\\n\\n" + shared_context.strip(). Return the
    text. The result must not depend on any order, tier, path or time, so it stays
    byte-identical across calls and the prompt cache applies."""
    text = SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip()
    extra = shared_context.strip()
    if extra:
        text += "\n\n## Shared context\n\n" + extra
    return text


def build_prompt(order: WorkOrder, cwd: Path, retry_feedback: str | None = None) -> str:
    """The user message for one attempt: the repository-root preamble, then the order, then
    the retry feedback (if retry_feedback is not None and retry_feedback.strip() is
    non-empty). Exact format in the order's `decision: prompt format` context item."""
    root = str(Path(cwd).resolve())
    parts = [
        f"Repository root: {root}",
        f"Start every Bash command with `cd {root} && `. "
        "Every path in the work order is relative to this root.",
        "## Work order",
        "```json\n" + order.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n```",
    ]
    if retry_feedback is not None and retry_feedback.strip():
        parts += ["## Retry feedback", retry_feedback.strip()]
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def _int(value: Any) -> int:
    return int(value) if value is not None else 0


def usage_from_result(message: ResultMessage | None) -> Usage:
    """Token counts and cost of one session, from its ResultMessage. Rules in the order's
    `decision: usage` context item. Usage() (all zeros) if message is None."""
    if message is None:
        return Usage()
    model_usage = message.model_usage
    has_model_usage = isinstance(model_usage, dict) and bool(model_usage)
    if has_model_usage:
        values = list(model_usage.values())
        input_tokens = sum(_int(v.get("inputTokens")) for v in values)
        output_tokens = sum(_int(v.get("outputTokens")) for v in values)
        cache_read = sum(_int(v.get("cacheReadInputTokens")) for v in values)
        cache_creation = sum(_int(v.get("cacheCreationInputTokens")) for v in values)
    else:
        raw = message.usage or {}
        input_tokens = _int(raw.get("input_tokens"))
        output_tokens = _int(raw.get("output_tokens"))
        cache_read = _int(raw.get("cache_read_input_tokens"))
        cache_creation = _int(raw.get("cache_creation_input_tokens"))
    if message.total_cost_usd is not None:
        cost = float(message.total_cost_usd)
    elif has_model_usage:
        cost = sum(float(v.get("costUSD") or 0.0) for v in model_usage.values())
    else:
        cost = 0.0
    return Usage(
        input_tokens=input_tokens,
        output_tokens=output_tokens,
        cache_read_tokens=cache_read,
        cache_creation_tokens=cache_creation,
        cost_usd=cost,
    )


class SdkWorker:
    """A Worker backed by the Claude Agent SDK: one query() session per attempt."""

    def __init__(self, shared_context: str = "", query_fn: QueryFn | None = None) -> None:
        """self.system_prompt = load_system_prompt(shared_context), computed once here.
        self._query = query_fn or query (tests pass a fake with the same keyword call shape:
        query_fn(prompt=<str>, options=<ClaudeAgentOptions>))."""
        self.system_prompt = load_system_prompt(shared_context)
        self._query: QueryFn = query_fn or query

    def options(self, order: WorkOrder, tier: Tier, cwd: Path) -> ClaudeAgentOptions:
        """The exact ClaudeAgentOptions for one attempt; field values in the order's
        `decision: SDK options` context item."""
        return ClaudeAgentOptions(
            model=MODEL_IDS[tier],
            system_prompt=self.system_prompt,
            tools=list(WORKER_TOOLS),
            allowed_tools=list(WORKER_TOOLS),
            permission_mode="acceptEdits",
            cwd=str(Path(cwd).resolve()),
            max_turns=order.budget.max_turns,
            setting_sources=[],
            strict_mcp_config=True,
            verbatim_prompts=True,
            env=dict(WORKER_ENV),
        )

    async def run(
        self, order: WorkOrder, tier: Tier, cwd: Path, retry_feedback: str | None = None
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Run one session and turn it into a WorkerResult; algorithm in the order's
        `decision: run algorithm` context item. Never raises for SDK or model failures
        (catches Exception, not BaseException, so cancellation still propagates)."""
        prompt = build_prompt(order, cwd, retry_feedback)
        options = self.options(order, tier, cwd)
        result_msg: ResultMessage | None = None
        last_text = ""
        error: str | None = None
        try:
            async for message in self._query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
                if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage) and message.parent_tool_use_id is None:
                    text = "".join(b.text for b in message.content if isinstance(b, TextBlock))
                    if text.strip():
                        last_text = text
                elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                    result_msg = message
        except Exception as err:  # not BaseException: cancellation must propagate
            error = f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"[:2000]

        if (
            result_msg is not None
            and isinstance(result_msg.result, str)
            and result_msg.result.strip()
        ):
            final_text = result_msg.result
        else:
            final_text = last_text
        report = parse_report(final_text)

        status: WorkerStatus
        if error is not None:
            status = "error"
        elif result_msg is None:
            status = "error"
            error = "session ended without a result message"
        elif result_msg.is_error:
            status = "error"
            error = f"result {result_msg.subtype}"
            if isinstance(result_msg.errors, list) and result_msg.errors:
                error += ": " + "; ".join(str(e) for e in result_msg.errors)
        elif report is None:
            status = "unknown"
        else:
            status = report.status

        result = WorkerResult(
            status=status,
            usage=usage_from_result(result_msg),
            num_turns=result_msg.num_turns if result_msg else 0,
            duration_ms=result_msg.duration_ms if result_msg else 0,
            session_id=result_msg.session_id if result_msg else None,
            final_text=final_text,
            error=error,
        )
        return apply_report(result, report)


FakeStep = (
    WorkerResult
    | BaseException
    | Callable[[WorkOrder, Tier, Path, str | None], WorkerResult | Awaitable[WorkerResult]]
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WorkerCall:
    """One recorded FakeWorker.run call."""

    order_id: str
    tier: Tier
    cwd: Path
    retry_feedback: str | None


class FakeWorkerExhausted(RuntimeError):
    """FakeWorker.run was called for an order with no scripted step left and no default."""


class FakeWorker:
    """A scriptable Worker for tests. Each order id has its own queue of steps; every run()
    call pops the next step for order.id."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        script: Mapping[str, Sequence[FakeStep]] | None = None,
        default: FakeStep | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Copy each sequence in `script` into a per-order list (later changes to the
        caller's sequences have no effect). `default` is used when an order's queue is empty.
        self.calls starts as an empty list[WorkerCall]."""
        self._queues: dict[str, list[FakeStep]] = {
            order_id: list(steps) for order_id, steps in (script or {}).items()
        }
        self._default = default
        self.calls: list[WorkerCall] = []

    def add(self, order_id: str, *steps: FakeStep) -> None:
        """Append steps to the end of order_id's queue (creating it if missing)."""
        self._queues.setdefault(order_id, []).extend(steps)

    def remaining(self, order_id: str) -> int:
        """Number of scripted steps still queued for order_id (0 if none). Ignores default."""
        return len(self._queues.get(order_id, []))

    async def run(
        self, order: WorkOrder, tier: Tier, cwd: Path, retry_feedback: str | None = None
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Append WorkerCall(order.id, tier, cwd, retry_feedback) to self.calls FIRST, then
        take the next step: pop the front of order.id's queue, or use `default` if the queue
        is empty or missing; if there is neither, raise
        FakeWorkerExhausted(f"no scripted step left for order {order.id}").
        - WorkerResult: return step.model_copy(deep=True).
        - BaseException instance: raise it.
        - callable: call step(order, tier, cwd, retry_feedback); if the return value is
          awaitable, await it; return the WorkerResult.
        A `default` step is never consumed: it is reused for every call that needs it."""
        self.calls.append(WorkerCall(order.id, tier, cwd, retry_feedback))
        queue = self._queues.get(order.id)
        if queue:
            step = queue.pop(0)
        elif self._default is not None:
            step = self._default
        else:
            raise FakeWorkerExhausted(f"no scripted step left for order {order.id}")
        if isinstance(step, WorkerResult):
            return step.model_copy(deep=True)
        if isinstance(step, BaseException):
            raise step
        value = step(order, tier, cwd, retry_feedback)
        if inspect.isawaitable(value):
            value = await value
        return value


def fake_result(
    status: WorkerStatus = "done",
    summary: str = "",
    files_changed: Sequence[str] = (),
    cost_usd: float = 0.0,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
) -> WorkerResult:
    """Shorthand for scripting FakeWorker: a WorkerResult with these fields, the files as a
    list, and Usage(input_tokens=..., output_tokens=..., cost_usd=...)."""
    return WorkerResult(
        status=status,
        summary=summary,
        files_changed=list(files_changed),
        usage=Usage(input_tokens=input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens, cost_usd=cost_usd),
    )

"""Reviewer: one read-only agent session that checks a task's diff against its work order."""

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from claude_agent_sdk import (
    AssistantMessage,
    ClaudeAgentOptions,
    ResultMessage,
    TextBlock,
    query,
)
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError

from harness.config import MODEL_IDS, Tier
from harness.models import Usage, WorkOrder
from harness.worker import WORKER_ENV, QueryFn, usage_from_result

ReviewVerdict = Literal["pass", "fail", "unknown", "error"]

REVIEWER_PROMPT_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / "prompts" / "reviewer_system.md"

REVIEWER_TOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("Read", "Glob", "Grep")

REVIEW_MAX_TURNS = 20

_JSON_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^```json[ \t]*\n(.*?)\n```[ \t]*$", re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)


class ReviewReport(BaseModel):
    """The final JSON block of a reviewer's reply. Unknown extra keys are ignored."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")

    verdict: Literal["pass", "fail"]
    reasons: list[str]


class ReviewResult(BaseModel):
    """What one review returns. Only verdict "fail" fails a task; "unknown" (no valid JSON
    block) and "error" (the session failed) are recorded but do not fail it."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    verdict: ReviewVerdict
    reasons: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    usage: Usage = Field(default_factory=Usage)
    final_text: str = ""
    error: str | None = None


@runtime_checkable
class Reviewer(Protocol):
    async def review(self, order: WorkOrder, diff: str, tier: Tier, cwd: Path) -> ReviewResult:
        """Review `diff` (the task's changes) against `order` on `tier`, with read-only
        access to the worktree `cwd`. Failures come back as verdict "error", never as an
        exception (cancellation still propagates)."""
        ...


def parse_verdict(text: str) -> ReviewReport | None:
    """Take the LAST fenced ```json block (same fence rules as harness.worker.parse_report:
    the _JSON_BLOCK regex above), json.loads its body and validate it as a ReviewReport.
    Return None if there is no block, the body is not valid JSON (catch ValueError and
    RecursionError), it is not a JSON object, or validation fails. Never raises."""
    try:
        matches = _JSON_BLOCK.findall(text)
    except TypeError:
        return None
    if not matches:
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(matches[-1])
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    try:
        return ReviewReport.model_validate(data)
    except ValidationError:
        return None


def load_reviewer_prompt() -> str:
    """Read REVIEWER_PROMPT_PATH (UTF-8) and strip trailing whitespace."""
    return REVIEWER_PROMPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip()


def build_review_prompt(order: WorkOrder, diff: str) -> str:
    """The user message: "## Work order", then the order as a ```json fenced block
    (order.model_dump_json(indent=2)), then "## Diff", then the diff as a ```diff fenced
    block. Exact format in the `decision: review prompt format` context item."""
    body = "(empty diff)" if diff.strip() == "" else diff.rstrip("\n")
    return (
        "## Work order\n\n```json\n"
        + order.model_dump_json(indent=2)
        + "\n```\n\n"
        + "## Diff\n\n```diff\n"
        + body
        + "\n```"
    )


class SdkReviewer:
    """A Reviewer backed by the Claude Agent SDK: one query() session per review."""

    def __init__(self, query_fn: QueryFn | None = None) -> None:
        """self.system_prompt = load_reviewer_prompt(), computed once here.
        self._query = query_fn or query (same keyword call shape as SdkWorker:
        query_fn(prompt=<str>, options=<ClaudeAgentOptions>))."""
        self.system_prompt = load_reviewer_prompt()
        self._query: QueryFn = query_fn or query

    def options(self, tier: Tier, cwd: Path) -> ClaudeAgentOptions:
        """The exact ClaudeAgentOptions for one review; values in the
        `decision: reviewer SDK options` context item."""
        return ClaudeAgentOptions(
            model=MODEL_IDS[tier],
            system_prompt=self.system_prompt,
            tools=list(REVIEWER_TOOLS),
            allowed_tools=list(REVIEWER_TOOLS),
            permission_mode="dontAsk",
            cwd=str(Path(cwd).resolve()),
            max_turns=REVIEW_MAX_TURNS,
            setting_sources=[],
            strict_mcp_config=True,
            verbatim_prompts=True,
            env=dict(WORKER_ENV),
        )

    async def review(self, order: WorkOrder, diff: str, tier: Tier, cwd: Path) -> ReviewResult:
        """Run one session; algorithm in the `decision: review algorithm` context item.
        Catches Exception (not BaseException), so cancellation propagates."""
        prompt = build_review_prompt(order, diff)
        options = self.options(tier, cwd)
        result_msg: ResultMessage | None = None
        last_text = ""
        error: str | None = None
        try:
            async for message in self._query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
                if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage) and message.parent_tool_use_id is None:
                    text = "".join(b.text for b in message.content if isinstance(b, TextBlock))
                    if text.strip():
                        last_text = text
                elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                    result_msg = message
        except Exception as err:  # not BaseException: cancellation must propagate
            error = f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"[:2000]

        if (
            result_msg is not None
            and isinstance(result_msg.result, str)
            and result_msg.result.strip()
        ):
            final_text = result_msg.result
        else:
            final_text = last_text

        verdict: ReviewVerdict
        reasons: list[str] = []
        if error is not None:
            verdict = "error"
        elif result_msg is None:
            verdict = "error"
            error = "session ended without a result message"
        elif result_msg.is_error:
            verdict = "error"
            error = f"result {result_msg.subtype}"
            if isinstance(result_msg.errors, list) and result_msg.errors:
                error += ": " + "; ".join(str(e) for e in result_msg.errors)
        else:
            report = parse_verdict(final_text)
            if report is None:
                verdict = "unknown"
            else:
                verdict = report.verdict
                reasons = list(report.reasons)

        return ReviewResult(
            verdict=verdict,
            reasons=reasons,
            usage=usage_from_result(result_msg),
            final_text=final_text,
            error=error,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReviewCall:
    """One recorded FakeReviewer.review call."""

    order_id: str
    diff: str
    tier: Tier
    cwd: Path


class FakeReviewer:
    """A scriptable Reviewer for tests: each review() call takes the next scripted step."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        steps: Sequence[ReviewResult | BaseException] = (),
        default: ReviewResult | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Copy `steps` into a list (later changes to the caller's sequence have no effect).
        `default` is used when the list is empty. self.calls starts as an empty
        list[ReviewCall]."""
        self._steps: list[ReviewResult | BaseException] = list(steps)
        self._default = default
        self.calls: list[ReviewCall] = []

    async def review(self, order: WorkOrder, diff: str, tier: Tier, cwd: Path) -> ReviewResult:
        """Append ReviewCall(order.id, diff, tier, cwd) to self.calls FIRST. Then pop the
        front step, or use `default` if no step is left; if there is neither, raise
        RuntimeError("no scripted review left"). A ReviewResult step is returned as
        step.model_copy(deep=True); an exception step is raised. `default` is never
        consumed."""
        self.calls.append(ReviewCall(order.id, diff, tier, cwd))
        if self._steps:
            step = self._steps.pop(0)
        elif self._default is not None:
            step = self._default
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("no scripted review left")
        if isinstance(step, BaseException):
            raise step
        return step.model_copy(deep=True)


def fake_review(
    verdict: ReviewVerdict = "pass", reasons: Sequence[str] = (), cost_usd: float = 0.0
) -> ReviewResult:
    """Shorthand for tests: ReviewResult(verdict=verdict, reasons=list(reasons),
    usage=Usage(cost_usd=cost_usd))."""
    return ReviewResult(verdict=verdict, reasons=list(reasons), usage=Usage(cost_usd=cost_usd))

Field added to both WorkerResult (src/harness/worker.py) and ReviewResult (src/harness/review.py), as the LAST field of each model:

    session_init: dict[str, Any] | None = None

It holds session_init_facts(<the first SDK SystemMessage with subtype 'init'>) of the session, or None when no init message arrived (FakeWorker/FakeReviewer results and fake_result()/fake_review() leave it None). Keys, in order: model, tools, skills, mcp_servers, permissionMode, apiKeySource. Values are copied as the SDK sent them (a missing key is None).

harness.worker also exports:

SESSION_INIT_KEYS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "model",
    "tools",
    "skills",
    "mcp_servers",
    "permissionMode",
    "apiKeySource",
)


def session_init_facts(message: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The SESSION_INIT_KEYS facts of an SDK init message: {key: message.data.get(key)} for
    every key, in SESSION_INIT_KEYS order (a missing key maps to None). None unless
    `message` is a SystemMessage whose subtype is "init" and whose data is a dict. Never
    raises."""
    if not isinstance(message, SystemMessage) or message.subtype != "init":
        return None
    if not isinstance(message.data, dict):
        return None
    return {key: message.data.get(key) for key in SESSION_INIT_KEYS}

from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence

StateCallback = Callable[[TaskState], Awaitable[None]]

REPLAN_FEEDBACK_LINES = 40


def tier_for_attempt(start: Tier, attempt: int) -> Tier:
    """The tier for 1-based `attempt` of an order whose tier is `start`: one step up
    TIER_LADDER per earlier attempt, staying at the top once there.
    TIER_LADDER[min(TIER_LADDER.index(start) + attempt - 1, len(TIER_LADDER) - 1)].
    Raises ValueError if attempt < 1."""
    if attempt < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"attempt must be >= 1, got {attempt}")
    return TIER_LADDER[min(TIER_LADDER.index(start) + attempt - 1, len(TIER_LADDER) - 1)]


def replan_note(order: WorkOrder, history: Sequence[AttemptRecord]) -> str:
    """The short note for a blocked task. Exact format in the `decision: replan note`
    context item."""
    tiers = ", ".join(r.tier for r in history)
    lines = [
        f"Task {order.id} is blocked after {len(history)} attempts (tiers: {tiers}); "
        "the last one ran on opus.",
        "Last verifier output:",
    ]
    if history and history[-1].feedback.strip():
        lines.extend(history[-1].feedback.splitlines()[:REPLAN_FEEDBACK_LINES])
    else:
        lines.append("(none)")
    lines.append(
        "Next step: re-plan this order. Split it, paste the missing context, or fix its "
        "acceptance commands."
    )
    return "\n".join(lines)


class Router:
    def __init__(
        self,
        worker: Worker,
        events: EventLog,
        *,
        reviewer: Reviewer | None = None,
        review_tier: Tier = "sonnet",
        timeout_s: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
        on_state: StateCallback | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store every argument on self under the same name (self.worker, self.events,
        self.reviewer, self.review_tier, self.timeout_s, self.on_state)."""
        self.worker = worker
        self.events = events
        self.reviewer = reviewer
        self.review_tier = review_tier
        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.on_state = on_state

    async def _changed(self, state: TaskState) -> None:
        """await self.on_state(state) if on_state is set; otherwise do nothing."""
        if self.on_state is not None:
            await self.on_state(state)

    async def route(
        self, order: WorkOrder, cwd: Path, state: TaskState, base: str = "HEAD"
    ) -> TaskState:
        """Run attempts of `order` in the worktree `cwd` until one passes verification or
        order.budget.max_attempts attempts are used. Mutates and returns `state` (the
        caller passes a fresh TaskState(task_id=order.id)). Algorithm, events and final
        states in the `decision: route algorithm` context item. Never raises except
        CancelledError."""

        async def emit(type_: str, payload: dict) -> None:
            await self.events.emit(type_, task_id=order.id, payload=payload)

        feedback: str | None = None
        prev_tier: Tier | None = None
        n = 0
        tier: Tier = order.tier
        for n in range(1, order.budget.max_attempts + 1):
            tier = tier_for_attempt(order.tier, n)
            if prev_tier is not None and tier != prev_tier:
                await emit("escalated", {"attempt": n, "from_tier": prev_tier, "to_tier": tier})

            state.status = "running"
            state.attempts = n
            state.tier_used = tier
            await self._changed(state)
            await emit("attempt_started", {"attempt": n, "tier": tier})

            try:
                result = await self.worker.run(order, tier, cwd, feedback)
            except Exception as err:
                result = WorkerResult(status="error", error=f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"[:2000])
            await emit(
                "worker_finished",
                {
                    "attempt": n,
                    "tier": tier,
                    "status": result.status,
                    "summary": result.summary,
                    "error": result.error,
                    "cost_usd": result.usage.cost_usd,
                    "input_tokens": result.usage.input_tokens,
                    "output_tokens": result.usage.output_tokens,
                    "num_turns": result.num_turns,
                    "duration_ms": result.duration_ms,
                },
            )

            state.status = "verifying"
            state.usage = state.usage.plus(result.usage)
            await self._changed(state)
            await emit("verify_started", {"attempt": n})

            vr = await verify(
                order,
                cwd,
                base=base,
                timeout_s=self.timeout_s,
                reviewer=self.reviewer,
                review_tier=self.review_tier,
            )
            review_usage = vr.review.usage if vr.review is not None else Usage()
            fb = format_feedback(vr)
            await emit(
                "verify_finished",
                {
                    "attempt": n,
                    "passed": vr.passed,
                    "failed_commands": [c.cmd for c in vr.commands if not c.passed],
                    "outside_files": vr.outside_files,
                    "scope_error": vr.scope_error,
                    "review_verdict": vr.review.verdict if vr.review is not None else None,
                    "review_reasons": vr.review.reasons if vr.review is not None else [],
                },
            )

            state.usage = state.usage.plus(review_usage)
            state.history.append(
                AttemptRecord(
                    attempt=n,
                    tier=tier,
                    worker_status=result.status,
                    passed=vr.passed,
                    usage=result.usage.plus(review_usage),
                    summary=result.summary,
                    feedback=fb,
                )
            )

            if vr.passed:
                state.status = "done"
                await self._changed(state)
                await emit(
                    "task_done", {"attempts": n, "tier": tier, "cost_usd": state.usage.cost_usd}
                )
                return state
            feedback = fb
            prev_tier = tier

        if tier == "opus":
            state.status = "blocked"
            state.replan_note = replan_note(order, state.history)
            await self._changed(state)
            await emit(
                "task_blocked", {"attempts": n, "tier": tier, "replan_note": state.replan_note}
            )
        else:
            state.status = "failed"
            state.error = f"budget exhausted after {n} attempts; last tier {tier}"
            await self._changed(state)
            await emit("task_failed", {"attempts": n, "tier": tier, "reason": state.error})
        return state

Field added to both WorkerResult (src/harness/worker.py) and ReviewResult (src/harness/review.py), as the LAST field of each model:

    session_init: dict[str, Any] | None = None

It holds session_init_facts(<the first SDK SystemMessage with subtype 'init'>) of the session, or None when no init message arrived (FakeWorker/FakeReviewer results and fake_result()/fake_review() leave it None). Keys, in order: model, tools, skills, mcp_servers, permissionMode, apiKeySource. Values are copied as the SDK sent them (a missing key is None).

harness.worker also exports:

SESSION_INIT_KEYS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "model",
    "tools",
    "skills",
    "mcp_servers",
    "permissionMode",
    "apiKeySource",
)


def session_init_facts(message: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The SESSION_INIT_KEYS facts of an SDK init message: {key: message.data.get(key)} for
    every key, in SESSION_INIT_KEYS order (a missing key maps to None). None unless
    `message` is a SystemMessage whose subtype is "init" and whose data is a dict. Never
    raises."""
    if not isinstance(message, SystemMessage) or message.subtype != "init":
        return None
    if not isinstance(message.data, dict):
        return None
    return {key: message.data.get(key) for key in SESSION_INIT_KEYS}

"""Planner behind `harness plan`: one interactive Opus session that runs the plan-project
skill until the user approves PROJECT_PLAN.md, then plan-stage on stage 1 until it writes a
plan.json that load_plan accepts."""

import asyncio
import hashlib
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from claude_agent_sdk import (
    AssistantMessage,
    ClaudeAgentOptions,
    ClaudeSDKClient,
    ResultMessage,
    TextBlock,
)
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from harness.config import MODEL_IDS
from harness.models import Usage
from harness.plan import PlanError, load_plan
from harness.worker import WORKER_ENV, usage_from_result

HARNESS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

PLANNER_SKILLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("plan-project", "plan-stage")

PLANNER_TOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "Bash")

PLANNER_MAX_TURNS = 80

PROJECT_PLAN_FILE = "PROJECT_PLAN.md"

STAGE_PLAN_DIR = Path("plans") / "stage-1"

MAX_ROUNDS = 20

MAX_FIX_ROUNDS = 2

APPROVED_RE = re.compile(r"^Status: approved \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$", re.MULTILINE)

PLANNER_APPEND = (
    "You are running headless inside `harness plan`. The user reads your replies as plain "
    "terminal text and answers by typing; ask questions and request approval in your reply "
    "text, then end your turn."
)

PROJECT_PROMPT = (
    "Use the plan-project skill to plan this project. Target repo: {repo}\n\n"
    "Project description:\n\n{description}"
)

STAGE_PROMPT = (
    "{project_plan} is approved. Now use the plan-stage skill on stage 1 of {project_plan}. "
    "Write plan.json and plan.md to {stage_dir}/ (exactly this directory). Run the skill's "
    "validation snippet before you finish."
)

FIX_PROMPT = (
    "`harness validate` rejected {plan_path}: {error}\n\n"
    "Fix the plan and write it again to the same path."
)


class PlannerError(RuntimeError):
    """The planner stopped without a valid plan. The message says why."""


class PlannerTurn(BaseModel):
    """One planner reply. `usage` is the session's running total so far (the SDK reports
    cumulative usage on every turn of a ClaudeSDKClient session), not this turn alone."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    text: str = ""
    usage: Usage = Field(default_factory=Usage)
    error: str | None = None


class PlanResult(BaseModel):
    """What run_planner produced."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    project_plan: Path
    plan_path: Path
    usage: Usage = Field(default_factory=Usage)
    rounds: int = 0


@runtime_checkable
class PlannerSession(Protocol):
    async def send(self, text: str) -> PlannerTurn:
        """Send one user message and return the planner's reply once its turn ends.
        Failures come back as PlannerTurn.error, never as an exception (cancellation still
        propagates)."""
        ...

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """End the session. Safe to call more than once, and before any send()."""
        ...


Ask = Callable[[str], str | None]
Say = Callable[[str], None]


def check_skills(root: Path = HARNESS_ROOT) -> None:
    """Raise PlannerError(f"planner skills not found under {root / '.claude' / 'skills'}")
    unless <root>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md exists for every name in PLANNER_SKILLS."""
    skills_dir = Path(root) / ".claude" / "skills"
    for name in PLANNER_SKILLS:
        if not (skills_dir / name / "SKILL.md").is_file():
            raise PlannerError(f"planner skills not found under {root / '.claude' / 'skills'}")


def is_approved(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if `text` has a line that is exactly `Status: approved YYYY-MM-DD`."""
    return APPROVED_RE.search(text) is not None


def _fingerprint(path: Path) -> str | None:
    """sha256 hex digest of the file's bytes, or None if it does not exist."""
    try:
        data = Path(path).read_bytes()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


class SdkPlannerSession:
    """A PlannerSession on one ClaudeSDKClient, connected on the first send()."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo: Path,
        client_factory: Callable[[ClaudeAgentOptions], Any] | None = None,
        harness_root: Path = HARNESS_ROOT,
    ) -> None:
        """self.repo = Path(repo).resolve(); self.harness_root = Path(harness_root).resolve();
        self._factory = client_factory or ClaudeSDKClient (called as
        factory(options=<ClaudeAgentOptions>)); self._client = None; self._usage = Usage()
        (the running total from the latest ResultMessage)."""
        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
        self.harness_root = Path(harness_root).resolve()
        self._factory = client_factory or ClaudeSDKClient
        self._client: Any = None
        self._usage = Usage()

    def options(self) -> ClaudeAgentOptions:
        """The exact options; values in the `decision: planner SDK options` context item."""
        return ClaudeAgentOptions(
            model=MODEL_IDS["opus"],
            system_prompt={"type": "preset", "preset": "claude_code", "append": PLANNER_APPEND},
            tools=[*PLANNER_TOOLS, "Skill"],
            allowed_tools=list(PLANNER_TOOLS),
            skills=list(PLANNER_SKILLS),
            setting_sources=["project"],
            add_dirs=[str(self.harness_root)],
            permission_mode="acceptEdits",
            cwd=str(self.repo),
            max_turns=PLANNER_MAX_TURNS,
            strict_mcp_config=True,
            env=dict(WORKER_ENV),
        )

    async def send(self, text: str) -> PlannerTurn:
        """Algorithm in the `decision: planner session` context item."""
        if self._client is None:
            client = self._factory(options=self.options())
            try:
                await client.connect()
            except Exception as err:
                return PlannerTurn(
                    usage=self._usage,
                    error=f"connect failed: {type(err).__name__}: {err}"[:2000],
                )
            self._client = client

        result_msg: ResultMessage | None = None
        last_text = ""
        error: str | None = None
        try:
            await self._client.query(text)
            async for message in self._client.receive_response():
                if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):
                    if message.parent_tool_use_id is None:
                        joined = "".join(
                            b.text for b in message.content if isinstance(b, TextBlock)
                        )
                        if joined.strip():
                            last_text = joined
                elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                    result_msg = message
        except Exception as err:
            error = f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"[:2000]

        if (
            result_msg is not None
            and isinstance(result_msg.result, str)
            and result_msg.result.strip()
        ):
            reply = result_msg.result
        else:
            reply = last_text

        if result_msg is not None:
            self._usage = usage_from_result(result_msg)

        if error is None:
            if result_msg is None:
                error = "turn ended without a result message"
            elif result_msg.is_error:
                error = f"result {result_msg.subtype}"
                errors = getattr(result_msg, "errors", None)
                if isinstance(errors, list) and errors:
                    error += ": " + "; ".join(str(e) for e in errors)

        return PlannerTurn(text=reply, usage=self._usage, error=error)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """If connected: await self._client.disconnect() (Exception ignored), then
        self._client = None."""
        if self._client is not None:
            try:
                await self._client.disconnect()
            except Exception:
                pass
            self._client = None


class FakePlannerSession:
    """A scripted PlannerSession for tests. Each send() takes the next step: a PlannerTurn
    (returned as a deep copy) or a callable (text) -> PlannerTurn, which may write files
    to simulate the planner's edits."""

    def __init__(self, steps: Sequence[PlannerTurn | Callable[[str], PlannerTurn]]) -> None:
        """Copy steps into a list. self.sent: list[str] = []; self.closed = False."""
        self._steps: list[PlannerTurn | Callable[[str], PlannerTurn]] = list(steps)
        self.sent: list[str] = []
        self.closed = False

    async def send(self, text: str) -> PlannerTurn:
        """Append text to self.sent FIRST, then pop and apply the front step. With no step
        left, raise RuntimeError("no scripted planner turn left")."""
        self.sent.append(text)
        if not self._steps:
            raise RuntimeError("no scripted planner turn left")
        step = self._steps.pop(0)
        if isinstance(step, PlannerTurn):
            return step.model_copy(deep=True)
        return step(text)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """self.closed = True."""
        self.closed = True


async def run_planner(
    description: str,
    repo: Path,
    session: PlannerSession,
    ask: Ask,
    say: Say,
    *,
    max_rounds: int = MAX_ROUNDS,
) -> PlanResult:
    """Drive both phases; algorithm in the `decision: planner flow` context item. Always
    closes the session (finally). Raises PlannerError when it stops without a valid plan."""
    repo = Path(repo).resolve()
    project_plan = repo / PROJECT_PLAN_FILE
    stage_dir = repo / STAGE_PLAN_DIR
    plan_path = stage_dir / "plan.json"
    rounds = 0
    usage = Usage()

    async def turn(msg: str) -> None:
        nonlocal rounds, usage
        rounds += 1
        if rounds > max_rounds:
            raise PlannerError(f"no valid plan after {max_rounds} rounds")
        t = await session.send(msg)
        usage = t.usage
        if t.text.strip():
            say(t.text)
        if t.error:
            raise PlannerError(f"planner session failed: {t.error}")

    async def answer() -> str:
        a = await asyncio.to_thread(ask, "> ")
        if a is None:

"""Git worktrees for parallel tasks: create, commit, merge back, clean up."""

import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

MergeResult = Literal["merged", "conflict"]


class WorktreeError(RuntimeError):
    """A git command failed in a way the caller must handle."""


def _git(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)


def _check(proc: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]) -> str:
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise WorktreeError(proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip())
    return proc.stdout


class WorktreeManager:
    def __init__(self, repo: Path, run_id: str, integration_branch: str = "main") -> None:
        self.repo = Path(repo)
        self.run_id = run_id
        self.integration_branch = integration_branch

    def branch(self, task_id: str) -> str:
        """harness/<run_id>/<task_id>"""
        return f"harness/{self.run_id}/{task_id}"

    def path(self, task_id: str) -> Path:
        """<repo>/.harness/worktrees/<task_id>"""
        return self.repo / ".harness" / "worktrees" / task_id

    def _ensure_excluded(self) -> None:
        out = _check(_git("rev-parse", "--git-common-dir", cwd=self.repo)).strip()
        common = Path(out)
        if not common.is_absolute():
            common = self.repo / common
        exclude = common / "info" / "exclude"
        exclude.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        existing = exclude.read_text() if exclude.exists() else ""
        if ".harness/" in existing.splitlines():
            return
        prefix = "" if not existing or existing.endswith("\n") else "\n"
        exclude.write_text(existing + prefix + ".harness/\n")

    def create(self, task_id: str, base: str | None = None) -> Path:
        """git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <base or integration_branch>. Raise WorktreeError
        (with git's stderr) if git fails, e.g. the branch or path already exists. Return the path.
        """
        self._ensure_excluded()
        path = self.path(task_id)
        _check(
            _git(
                "worktree",
                "add",
                "-b",
                self.branch(task_id),
                str(path),
                base or self.integration_branch,
                cwd=self.repo,
            )
        )
        return path

    def commit(self, task_id: str, message: str) -> bool:
        """git add -A, then commit in the worktree. Return False (and commit nothing) if there
        are no staged changes (`git diff --cached --quiet` exits 0), True after committing."""
        wt = self.path(task_id)
        _check(_git("add", "-A", cwd=wt))
        diff = _git("diff", "--cached", "--quiet", cwd=wt)
        if diff.returncode == 0:
            return False
        if diff.returncode != 1:
            raise WorktreeError(diff.stderr.strip())
        _check(_git("commit", "-m", message, cwd=wt))
        return True

    def merge(self, task_id: str) -> MergeResult:
        """In the worktree: git rebase <integration_branch>. On failure: git rebase --abort and
        return "conflict". Then in <repo>: git merge --ff-only <branch>; raise WorktreeError if
        that fails. Return "merged"."""
        wt = self.path(task_id)
        status = _check(_git("status", "--porcelain", cwd=wt))
        if status.strip():
            raise WorktreeError(f"uncommitted changes in {task_id}")
        rebase = _git("rebase", self.integration_branch, cwd=wt)
        if rebase.returncode != 0:
            _git("rebase", "--abort", cwd=wt)
            return "conflict"
        _check(_git("merge", "--ff-only", self.branch(task_id), cwd=self.repo))
        return "merged"

    def discard(self, task_id: str) -> None:
        """Remove this task's worktree and branch if they exist, so the task can start over.
        Every git failure here is ignored (the worktree or branch may not exist)."""
        path = self.path(task_id)
        _git("worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path), cwd=self.repo)
        _git("branch", "-D", self.branch(task_id), cwd=self.repo)
        _git("worktree", "prune", cwd=self.repo)
        if path.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(path)

    def cleanup(self) -> None:
        """Remove this run's worktrees and branches and nothing of other runs: git worktree
        remove --force every worktree under <repo>/.harness/worktrees whose branch (from
        `git worktree list --porcelain`) is under refs/heads/harness/<run_id>/, delete every
        branch under refs/heads/harness/<run_id>/ (git branch -D), then git worktree prune."""
        root = (self.repo / ".harness" / "worktrees").resolve()
        prefix = f"refs/heads/harness/{self.run_id}/"
        listing = _check(_git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain", cwd=self.repo))
        for record in listing.split("\n\n"):
            path: str | None = None
            branch: str | None = None
            for line in record.splitlines():
                if line.startswith("worktree "):
                    path = line[len("worktree ") :]
                elif line.startswith("branch "):
                    branch = line[len("branch ") :]
            if path is None or branch is None or not branch.startswith(prefix):
                continue
            wt = Path(path).resolve()
            if root in wt.parents:
                _check(_git("worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt), cwd=self.repo))
        refs = _check(
            _git(
                "for-each-ref",
                "--format=%(refname:short)",
                f"refs/heads/harness/{self.run_id}/",
                cwd=self.repo,
            )
        )
        for name in refs.split():
            _check(_git("branch", "-D", name, cwd=self.repo))
        _check(_git("worktree", "prune", cwd=self.repo))
